title: The MDS conjecture over finite fields of even order
abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the linear MDS conjecture for every finite field of even order. For a finite field K with an even number q of elements and 2 ≤ k ≤ q, the maximum length of a k-dimensional linear maximum distance separable (MDS) code over K is q + 2 when k = 3 or k = q − 1, and q + 1 otherwise; codes are subspaces of K^N and an MDS code is one whose minimum Hamming distance equals N − k + 1. The upper bound is proved through the correspondence between MDS codes and arcs: after puncturing and duality it suffices to exclude arcs of q + 2 vectors in K^r for 4 ≤ r ≤ q/2 + 1. A hypothetical such arc gives one plane arc together with r − 3 lifts that, with three coordinate rows, form r linearly independent vectors; the formalization proves that all lifts of a plane arc lie in one common subspace of dimension at most r − 1. The proof uses an exactly normalized form of Segre's envelope of the tangents, a characteristic-two derivative obstruction, and a dimension bound for a colon ideal of (X^n, Y^n, Z^n) with n = q/2. Extended Reed–Solomon codes and the regular hyperoval show that the bound is attained.
